notes.title: Stockpile update: Temple showcase
notes.content:
The upcoming [b]Stockpile[/b] update contains several thousand changes, improvements, additions, and fixes to the game, engine, and servers of Gods and Idols. But that's not all – this update also brings exciting [b]new gameplay mechanics[/b], and today I am revealing: the Temple.

[h2]The Temple[/h2]
The Temple is a powerful late-game building that harnesses the energy of your Population to create Miracles. Two key Miracles available in the Temple are [b]Faithful Prayer[/b] and [b]Scry[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/10983461/4ff3e822a01ff13771655012bbeeea5ca4971d60.png[/img]
[h2]Faithful Prayer[/h2]
When the [b]Faithful Prayer[/b] Miracle is active, it generates a new resource called [b]Faith[/b]. Faith is used to create Accretions and Planets after your first one. As your system grows and more planets are added, the amount of Faith required to create additional Accretions increases.

However, Faith has a high Decay rate, so multiple Temples working together will be required to maintain high Faith reserves.

Only unemployed Population can contribute to Faithful Prayer, and the amount of Faith generated is directly proportional to the number of unemployed Population available.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/10983461/87cb4e49c0b1598ba755b8e3f6b81358e4fd399f.png[/img]
[h2]Scry[/h2]
The Scry Miracle comes in three variants: [b]Metal[/b], [b]Life[/b], and [b]Gas[/b]. Scrying in a Temple takes time and consumes both Faith and Shards. And upon completion will permanently increase the chosen Planet stat.

Scrying can only increase a Planet stat to a maximum of 100. For those looking to go beyond this limit, you'll need to wait for [REDACTED], which will be introduced in the second planned update: [b]Limbo[/b].

And why would you want to increase a Planet's stats? Well, that's because of a new mechanic – [REDACTED] – which will be revealed in the third planned update: [b]Logistics[/b].

One major change in the upcoming update is that stockpiles will provide a number of "slots" that can be reserved for specific resources, providing stockpile space for those resources.

There are still planet-wide global +Stockpile modifiers for certain buildings, such as the Citadel.

notes.title: Patch 5.25.751 (Workers, Visuals, and more)
notes.content:
This has turned out to be the largest patch to date, with several major features added to the game.
Not to mention the amount of fixes, tweaks, and improvements to several key systems and mechanics.
Almost 120 thousand additional lines of code have been written for the client and server, as well as several new assets created.
To summarize it succinctly would be impossible, so keep reading the change notes below for all the juicy details!

[*]Farms no longer have any base production

[*]Strength of the attack depend on amount of stockpiled resources and defenses
[*]Ravager scouts appear roughly once per hour and remain near the planet for 15 to 30 minutes
[*]Ravager scouts deal no damage, but if not destroyed in time will leave and report back to the Ravager fleet
[*]Ravager attack fleets are more likely to occur for each scout that have reported back since the last attack
[*]Destroy Ravager scouts to reduce the likelyhood of a Ravager attack fleet

notes.title: Developer update
notes.content:
[b]Patches and updates are changing[/b]
As the scope of the upcoming patch grows it has become evident that it will take some more time to get ready.
In order to avoid a repeat of the dreaded "Phase III coming soon!" I have decided to make some major changes in how I approach updates, as well as how to involve you deities more in the process.

The first major change is that upcoming patch notes will now be referred to as the Immediate Roadmap.
All features and items on the Immediate Roadmap are actively being worked on.
The second major change is that any feature on the Immediate Roadmap that becomes ready will immediately be pushed out as an update instead of waiting for the "whole" patch.

Some features rely on other features, and in those cases the base features simply have to become ready first.

[b]Vote for the features you want me to focus on[/b]
The third major change is that I am adding an ingame voting system, where you will be able to cast your vote for which feature (Or features) you would like me to focus on.

The duration the vote covers may change, but I am going to try to keep it weekly.

You can vote for multiple options, or several times for the same option.
Every active player gets one free vote per week. Additional votes cost Essence. You will be able to make Essence ingame without spending any money, and I will be adding the ingame shop soon where you'll also be able to purchase Essence.
You will be able to vote multiple times during the same period, regardless of if you buy Essence or gain it via gameplay.

Importantly, this is just a vote for what you'd like me to focus on, it is not a vote to discard features or adding one feature in favor of another. All features and options shown during votes will be things that are going to make it into the game, the question is just about the order of things.

[b]But why?[/b]
This accomplishes several goals, first it keeps me focused on the things you deities actually want to see, not just what I find the most fun to work on.
Second, I hope this will bring in some much needed money that can be spent on artwork, models, etc (And of course programmer-fuel: Energy drinks)
And most importantly it should hopefully produce more frequent updates of substance as I will push features live as soon as they become ready instead of as part of a larger update.


As always your feedback is important, let me know if you have any questions and I'll do my best to answer them.

notes.title: "Foundation" new things
notes.content:
[h1]Electricity[/h1]
Among the new buildings coming in the Foundation patch are the power plants.
Several types will be available, using a variety of different fuels (Or in some cases no fuel)
Production buildings that have power will produce goods faster and more efficiently than buildings without power.

[h1]Fleet upkeep[/h1]
As you build ships they start docked in the shipyard. 
Docked ships require very little upkeep, and no fuel or food.
Once you assign the docked ships to a fleet, they start requiring several goods in order to function at full efficiency.
For example, munitions and fuel are important to keep a fleet battle-ready, oxygen and MRE packs are required to keep the crew happy, and fuel is required for the fleet to move at full speed.
Note that even without any supplies, fleets will still move and do battle, just very poorly.

No screenshots this week, but expect some fancy ones next time!

notes.title: Upcoming patch
notes.content:
I apologize for the lack of updates, I honestly forgot to make a post.
I am all healed up since the appendix mess, and have been working on the upcoming patch for a few weeks now.

The patch brings some pretty massive changes to the way buildings are constructed. No longer will you place individual buildings on the planet. Instead you will place a "City" with a limited number of places where you can construct specific buildings. As the city population grows, more building slots will open up.

The goal of this change is to make it more fun to manage your planet. Watching your city, or cities, grow beats looking at a bunch of random buildings.
It will also mean some information becomes much clearer, for example population statuses and what is affecting them.

In addition buildings will now affect other nearby buildings, for example: placing a factory right next to a farm will have negative consequences for the farms productivity.

Another new system is the Unique resources. They will replace the currently unused "Planet bonus #". The patch will launch with a handful of Unique resources, and the plan is to add more later. The Unique resources will provide various bonuses ranging from simply being another source of raw materials such as Iron, all the way to empire-wide bonuses. To use them you will need to construct a new building, the Laboratory.
And of course you will be able to trade Unique resources.

And last but not least, military ships will finally become available.
You will be able to construct fighters, and carriers to transport them around. Form fleets, and send them on missions in the asteroid belts/planets/space.
These missions will be how you get Artifacts in the future. However Artifacts will not be in this patch as they need to be updated for the new City system.
You will also not be able to send fleets to other star systems in this update. But if there are multiple people in the same system you will be able to have your fleets do combat.

notes.title: Upcoming patch
notes.content:
I apologize for the lack of updates, I honestly forgot to make a post.
I am all healed up since the appendix mess, and have been working on the upcoming patch for a few weeks now.

The patch brings some pretty massive changes to the way buildings are constructed. No longer will you place individual buildings on the planet. Instead you will place a "City" with a limited number of places where you can construct specific buildings. As the city population grows, more building slots will open up.

The goal of this change is to make it more fun to manage your planet. Watching your city, or cities, grow beats looking at a bunch of random buildings.
It will also mean some information becomes much clearer, for example population statuses and what is affecting them.

In addition buildings will now affect other nearby buildings, for example: placing a factory right next to a farm will have negative consequences for the farms productivity.

Another new system is the Unique resources. They will replace the currently unused "Planet bonus #". The patch will launch with a handful of Unique resources, and the plan is to add more later. The Unique resources will provide various bonuses ranging from simply being another source of raw materials such as Iron, all the way to empire-wide bonuses. To use them you will need to construct a new building, the Laboratory.
And of course you will be able to trade Unique resources.

And last but not least, military ships will finally become available.
You will be able to construct fighters, and carriers to transport them around. Form fleets, and send them on missions in the asteroid belts/planets/space.
These missions will be how you get Artifacts in the future. However Artifacts will not be in this patch as they need to be updated for the new City system.
You will also not be able to send fleets to other star systems in this update. But if there are multiple people in the same system you will be able to have your fleets do combat.
